body: This is the direction that matters and the one the compression post-mortem says to write first: their bytes, our reader. A verifier exercised only against a signer we also wrote proves that two halves agree, which is not the question anybody is asking of a certificate.

author: reek
body: The positive: OpenSSL's signature over OpenSSL's message.

author: reek
body: A signature with one byte disturbed. It is still the right length and still a number below the modulus, so nothing but the arithmetic and the padding comparison can reject it.

author: reek
body: The right signature against a different message. This is the forgery that matters: the padding is genuine and only the digest differs.

author: reek
body: The altered byte is produced by flipping a bit of the original rather than by writing a literal. The first draft set byte zero to 99, and the message begins with `c`, which IS 99 -- so the "different" message was the same message and the case reported True. A control that quietly tests nothing is worse here than no control, because this is the line that would report a forgery as genuine. Derive the difference; do not assert it.

author: reek
body: A truncated signature, refused on width before any arithmetic runs.
